sources.title: IMENA IN PRIIMKI, ROJSTNI DNEVI — metodološko pojasnilo
Avtorske pravice
sources.note: SURS permits reuse, adaptation, and commercial use with attribution; identify your own derived calculations. The general permission does not cover third-party visual assets.

methodology: This is a public aggregate inventory of first names of residents of Slovenia. It is not an ethnic, nationality, or native-language whitelist and is not every name used in Slovenia.
Resident figures refer to 1 January 2026. Newborn figures refer to live births in 2025, published 23 June 2026. These are separate populations and must never share one unlabeled popularity rank.

The resident public table inventory includes a name-sex category only when it reached at least five in any observed year of the full historical series (2008–2026). Therefore a current '-' does not mean the name was used by five people in 2026.
A source '-' means fewer than five OR no occurrence in the selected year. JSON count/rank nulls and raw '-' are preserved; never zero-fill, infer the suppressed value, or describe it as absent.
A missing name-sex combination from a public table has status not_in_public_table_inventory and must not be treated as a confirmed zero.

Names retain original spelling, diacritics, spaces, and hyphens. SURS treats each multiword first name as one indivisible name; do not split Ana Marija into two observations or collapse Ana Marija and Ana-Marija.

Rows are merged into a page candidate only by exact name string (Unicode NFC for stable identifiers). Male and female observations remain separate. The same page and all five main design families apply to every person with that name; each family offers three genuinely distinct layouts, making fifteen downloadable designs with paired PDF and WebP outputs per selected year.
All ranks here are source-provided sex-specific national ranks. Ties are retained. Candidate order is an editorial prioritization and is not an official combined-sex national rank.
Priority fills use the largest disclosed resident sex-specific count, not inferred totals. Website search demand was not measured; name prevalence is not SEO search volume.

Latest product scope: five main design families × three genuinely distinct layouts = fifteen downloadable designs. The 8,561 name-page candidates produce 128,415 name/design combinations per calendar year; each design has one PDF and one WebP. Four supported years (2027–2030) therefore allow 1,027,320 binary files, excluding thumbnails and extra print sizes. There remains one canonical HTML page per exact name; these design/file totals are capacity scenarios, not published pages or existing files.
Every candidate requires editorial, calendar-rendering, font, download, and indexing quality gates before publication. No page is marked ready or published by this research.

The launch set is the union of resident rank <=75 in each sex and newborn rank <=25 in each sex, deduplicated by exact name, then filled to exactly 200 by largest published resident count. The 1,000-name growth set retains the 200 and adds the highest remaining published-count candidates.

slug_policy.recommended_name_id: si_ + first 12 hexadecimal SHA-256 characters of exact NFC UTF-8 name; verify uniqueness at import (verified for this inventory).
slug_policy.canonical_slug_proposal: ascii_slug_base + '-' + name_id; same URL regardless of the sex record, stable across years. An alternative is a registered Unicode slug that preserves exact names; do not blindly remove accents.
slug_policy.ascii_slug_base_algorithm: Explicit transliteration of đ,ł,ð,ø,æ,œ,ß,þ,ı; Unicode NFKD; remove combining marks; lowercase; any remaining non-ASCII alphanumeric becomes uHEX; other separators become hyphens. The collision counts below are specific to this definition.

examples.note: Both are disclosed current names; preserve two identities and pages.
Saša appears in both sex tables and must be one page with separate statistics; Sasa is a separate historical male category with '-' for 2026, not a current disclosed candidate.
Space and hyphen are distinct official names; slug normalization must not merge them.

name_day_research.scope: Personalized printable calendar with a person's name is a product distinct from a godovni koledar / godovi (name-day calendar). SURS gives frequencies, not religious name-day mappings.
name_day_research.product_label_recommendation: Koledar z imenom; page heading example: Ana – koledar za tiskanje. These are proposed localized labels, not measured SEO volume claims.
name_day_research.data_model_recommendation: Keep optional name-day records separate with name_id, month, day, saint_or_tradition, source_url, source_date, confidence, reviewer, and display_status. Allow multiple dated records per name. Null/unverified is allowed; do not invent one date per name.

sources.finding: The publisher's own presentation of Simon Lenarčič's guide describes possible patrons/days per baptismal name and contrasts church and folk calendars, including changes in dates and names.
Example verified source: Saint Ana and Joahim are observed together on 26 July under the calendar effective from 1969; the source distinguishes Joahim's earlier 16 August date.
The official Slovenian Catholic site documents adding Marija and Lazar alongside Marta on 29 July. This demonstrates why saint identity, tradition and dated source matter.

name_day_research.limitations: No comprehensive licensed Slovenian name-day dataset acquired. Do not copy a competitor's full calendar or assign a name-day to every frequency name. Verify source/reuse terms and individual variants before optional display. Keep this feature optional for launch.
